title: The Frontier of Spatial Intelligence with Fei-Fei Li

reader_summary.headline: This is fundamentally philosophically to be a different problem.
reader_summary.overview: This is fundamentally philosophically to be a different problem. The previous decade had mostly been about understanding data that already exists. But the next decade was going to be about understanding new data. Visual spatial intelligence is so fundamental, it's as fundamental as language.

key_points.text: It is like unwrapping presence on Christmas, that every day you know there's going to be some amazing new discovery.
key_points.evidence_quote: It is like unwrapping presence on Christmas, that every day you know there's going to be some amazing new discovery, some amazing new application or algorithm somewhere.

key_points.text: If we see something or if we imagine something, both can converge towards generating it.
key_points.evidence_quote: If we see something or if we imagine something, both can converge towards generating it.

key_points.text: I think we're in the middle of a Cambrian explosion.

key_points.text: The next chapter of AI isn't about better language models.
key_points.evidence_quote: The next chapter of AI isn't about better language models.

thesis: The podcast argues that the next decade of AI is defined by spatial intelligence, which is as fundamental as language, rather than improvements to existing language models. This shift represents a 'Cambrian explosion' where the field moves from understanding static data to generating and understanding new 3D worlds, pixels, videos, and audio to achieve true machine intelligence.
